title: Correct fibre dimension of n variables and c equations gives flatness near the prime
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $N\ge c\ge0$ integers, $g_1,\dots,g_c\in R[y_1,\dots,y_N]$ and $S=R[y_1,\dots,y_N]/(g_1,\dots,g_c)$. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal, $\mathfrak p\subset R$ its inverse image, $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ the residue fields and $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; let $\mathfrak Q\subset F$ be the kernel of the ring map $F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar s\bar\lambda$ (a prime ideal). Assume that the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}F$ at the point $\mathfrak Q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] equals $N-c$. Then there is $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that the localization $S_g$ is a flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; consequently the localization $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$ and the local ring map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00ST (lemma-localize-relative-complete-intersection, line 36671), part (3) (S_g is a relative global complete intersection, Definition Tag 00SP, line 36506), with Lemma Tag 00SW (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection, line 36843: a relative global complete intersection is syntomic, i.e. flat) and Definition Tag 00QD (definition-relative-dimension: dim_q(S/R)); the step of Smoothing 07CP (line 1577) 'R -> D_k is syntomic at q_k by our count of the number of equations'

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-dimension-neighborhood], applied with $d=N-c$ to the finite type $R$-algebra $S$ (generated by the classes of $y_1,\dots,y_N$), choose $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that every nonempty fibre of $S_g$ has dimension at most $N-c$. Choose a polynomial lift $h$ of $g$. Put $T=R[y_1,\dots,y_N,z]/(g_1,\dots,g_c,hz-1)$. The map $T\to S_g$ sends $z$ to $g^{-1}$ and the old variables to their classes. Conversely the class of $h$ in $T$ is invertible with inverse $z$, so [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] gives $S_g\to T$. These maps are inverse on every old variable and on $z$, hence inverse. For each prime $\mathfrak p'\subset R$, polynomial scalar extension [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] and quotient base change [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] identify its fibre with $\kappa(\mathfrak p')[y_1,\dots,y_N,z]/(\bar g_1,\dots,\bar g_c,\bar h z-1)$. If nonzero, its dimension is at least $(N+1)-(c+1)=N-c$ by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-quotient-dimension-lower-bound], and at most $N-c$ by the choice of $g$. Thus the presentation of $T\cong S_g$ is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00ST (current label Lemma 10.136.10), proof part (3), using Tag 00QH and the dimension bound for polynomial quotients

proof.text: A relative global complete intersection is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-flat], which is precisely Stacks Tag 00SW. Therefore S_g is flat over R.

Since $g\notin\mathfrak q$, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization] identifies $S_{\mathfrak q}$ as the localization of $S_g$ at the image of $S\setminus\mathfrak q$: the composite inverts exactly these denominators, and every fraction has denominator in that set. It is flat over $S_g$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. It is consequently flat over $R$: for an injection $U\to V$ of $R$-modules, flatness of $S_g$ gives an injection $U\otimes_RS_g\to V\otimes_RS_g$, and flatness of $S_{\mathfrak q}$ over $S_g$ preserves this injection after tensoring; associativity identifies the result with $U\otimes_RS_{\mathfrak q}\to V\otimes_RS_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Finally apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] to the flat map $R\to S_g$ at $\mathfrak qS_g$ to obtain flatness of $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_flat_away_of_fibre_dimension_eq (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (N c : ℕ) (hc : c ≤ N) (equations : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin N) R) : let S := MvPolynomial (Fin N) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range equations) ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S, let p := PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) q let Q := PrimeSpectrum.preimageEquivFiber R S p ⟨q, rfl⟩ topologicalKrullDimAt Q = ((N - c : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) → (∃ g : S, g ∉ q.asIdeal ∧ Module.Flat R (Localization.Away g)) ∧ Module.Flat R (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) ∧ (Localization.localRingHom p.asIdeal q.asIdeal (algebraMap R S) rfl).Flat
